import ast
import json
import math
import re
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

import chromadb

from lfx.custom.custom_component.component import Component
from lfx.io import StrInput, IntInput, Output, MultilineInput
from lfx.schema.dataframe import DataFrame


class HybridChromaDBQuery(Component):
    display_name = "Hybrid Vector Store"
    description = (
        "Perform semantic, keyword, hybrid, and hashtag-filtered retrieval "
        "over ATLAS Knowledge Base entries stored in ChromaDB."
    )
    documentation: str = "https://docs.langflow.org/components-custom-components"
    icon = "search"
    name = "HybridChromaDBQuery"

    inputs = [
        MultilineInput(
            name="queries",
            display_name="Queries",
            info="Newline-separated queries to search for.",
            value="",
            tool_mode=True,
        ),
        StrInput(
            name="collection_name",
            display_name="Collection Name",
            required=True,
        ),
        StrInput(
            name="persistence_path",
            display_name="Persistence Path",
            required=True,
        ),
        IntInput(
            name="n_results",
            display_name="Number of Final Results",
            value=5,
            tool_mode=True,
        ),
        StrInput(
            name="search_mode",
            display_name="Search Mode",
            info="One of: semantic, keyword, hybrid, tag_filtered_semantic.",
            value="hybrid",
            tool_mode=True,
        ),
        IntInput(
            name="candidate_pool",
            display_name="Candidate Pool Size",
            info=(
                "Number of semantic candidates to retrieve before reranking. "
                "Use a value larger than n_results for hybrid search."
            ),
            value=25,
            advanced=True,
        ),
        MultilineInput(
            name="keyword_terms",
            display_name="Keyword Terms",
            info=(
                "Optional newline-separated keyword terms. "
                "If empty, keywords are derived from each query."
            ),
            value="",
            tool_mode=True,
            advanced=True,
        ),
        StrInput(
            name="keyword_operator",
            display_name="Keyword Operator",
            info="Use 'any' or 'all' for keyword matching.",
            value="any",
            advanced=True,
        ),
        MultilineInput(
            name="hashtags",
            display_name="Hashtags",
            info=(
                "Optional newline-separated hashtags to filter by. "
                "Example: #entity/technique"
            ),
            value="",
            tool_mode=True,
            advanced=True,
        ),
        StrInput(
            name="hashtag_operator",
            display_name="Hashtag Operator",
            info="Use 'any' or 'all' for hashtag metadata filtering.",
            value="any",
            advanced=True,
        ),
        StrInput(
            name="metadata_where",
            display_name="Metadata Where Filter",
            info=(
                "Optional JSON/Python dict for Chroma metadata filtering. "
                "Example: {\"entity\": \"technique\"}"
            ),
            value="{}",
            advanced=True,
        ),
        StrInput(
            name="semantic_weight",
            display_name="Semantic Weight",
            info="Hybrid weighting for semantic rank.",
            value="0.65",
            advanced=True,
        ),
        StrInput(
            name="keyword_weight",
            display_name="Keyword Weight",
            info="Hybrid weighting for keyword rank.",
            value="0.35",
            advanced=True,
        ),
        IntInput(
            name="max_keyword_scan",
            display_name="Max Keyword Scan",
            info=(
                "Maximum number of records to scan locally for keyword scoring. "
                "For small ATLAS collections, this can safely be high."
            ),
            value=5000,
            advanced=True,
        ),
        StrInput(
            name="dedupe_by",
            display_name="Dedupe By",
            info="Use 'chroma_id' for chunk-level results or 'id' for ATLAS entity-level results.",
            value="chroma_id",
            advanced=True,
        ),
    ]

    outputs = [
        Output(
            display_name="DataFrame",
            name="results",
            method="build_output",
        ),
    ]

    STOPWORDS = {
        "a", "an", "and", "are", "as", "at", "be", "by", "for", "from",
        "how", "in", "is", "it", "of", "on", "or", "that", "the", "this",
        "to", "what", "when", "where", "which", "who", "with"
    }

    METADATA_TEXT_FIELDS = [
        "id",
        "entity",
        "name",
        "description",
        "url",
        "framework",
        "hashtags_text",
        "PARENT_TACTICS",
        "PARENT_TECHNIQUES",
        "PARENT_MITIGATIONS",
        "PARENT_CASESTUDIES",
        "CHILD_TECHNIQUES",
    ]

    RELATIONSHIP_COLUMNS = [
        "PARENT_TACTICS",
        "PARENT_TECHNIQUES",
        "PARENT_MITIGATIONS",
        "PARENT_CASESTUDIES",
        "CHILD_TECHNIQUES",
    ]

    def _parse_lines(self, value: Any) -> list[str]:
        if value is None:
            return []

        text = str(value).strip()
        if not text:
            return []

        lines = []
        for line in text.splitlines():
            item = line.strip()
            if item:
                lines.append(item)

        return lines

    def _parse_float(self, value: Any, default: float) -> float:
        try:
            return float(str(value).strip())
        except Exception:
            return default

    def _parse_where(self, value: Any) -> dict | None:
        if value is None:
            return None

        if isinstance(value, dict):
            return value or None

        text = str(value).strip()
        if not text or text == "{}":
            return None

        try:
            parsed = json.loads(text)
        except Exception:
            try:
                parsed = ast.literal_eval(text)
            except Exception as e:
                msg = f"metadata_where must be a JSON object or Python dict string: {e!s}"
                raise ValueError(msg) from e

        if not isinstance(parsed, dict):
            msg = "metadata_where must parse to a dictionary."
            raise ValueError(msg)

        return parsed or None

    def _normalize_hashtag(self, tag: str) -> str:
        tag = str(tag).strip()
        if not tag:
            return ""

        if not tag.startswith("#"):
            tag = f"#{tag}"

        return tag

    def _build_hashtag_where(self, hashtags: list[str], operator: str) -> dict | None:
        normalized = [self._normalize_hashtag(tag) for tag in hashtags]
        normalized = [tag for tag in normalized if tag]

        if not normalized:
            return None

        clauses = [{"hashtags": {"$contains": tag}} for tag in normalized]

        if len(clauses) == 1:
            return clauses[0]

        operator = str(operator or "any").strip().lower()

        if operator == "all":
            return {"$and": clauses}

        return {"$or": clauses}

    def _merge_where(self, first: dict | None, second: dict | None) -> dict | None:
        if first and second:
            return {"$and": [first, second]}

        return first or second

    def _derive_keywords(self, query: str) -> list[str]:
        hashtags = re.findall(r"#[A-Za-z0-9_./:-]+", query)
        words = re.findall(r"[A-Za-z0-9_.:-]+", query)

        terms = []
        for item in hashtags + words:
            item = item.strip()
            if not item:
                continue

            lowered = item.lower()
            if lowered in self.STOPWORDS:
                continue

            if len(lowered) < 3 and not item.startswith("#"):
                continue

            if item not in terms:
                terms.append(item)

        return terms

    def _build_where_document(self, keywords: list[str], operator: str) -> dict | None:
        keywords = [str(term).strip() for term in keywords if str(term).strip()]
        if not keywords:
            return None

        clauses = [{"$contains": term} for term in keywords]

        if len(clauses) == 1:
            return clauses[0]

        operator = str(operator or "any").strip().lower()

        if operator == "all":
            return {"$and": clauses}

        return {"$or": clauses}

    def _metadata_to_text(self, metadata: dict) -> str:
        parts = []

        for field in self.METADATA_TEXT_FIELDS:
            value = metadata.get(field)
            if value is None:
                continue

            if isinstance(value, list):
                parts.extend(str(item) for item in value)
            else:
                parts.append(str(value))

        hashtags = metadata.get("hashtags")
        if isinstance(hashtags, list):
            parts.extend(str(tag) for tag in hashtags)
        elif hashtags:
            parts.append(str(hashtags))

        return " ".join(parts)

    def _keyword_score(
        self,
        query: str,
        document: str,
        metadata: dict,
        keywords: list[str],
        operator: str,
    ) -> tuple[float, list[str]]:
        haystack = f"{document or ''} {self._metadata_to_text(metadata)}"
        haystack_lower = haystack.lower()

        name_lower = str(metadata.get("name", "")).lower()
        id_lower = str(metadata.get("id", "")).lower()
        entity_lower = str(metadata.get("entity", "")).lower()

        matched = []
        score = 0.0

        for term in keywords:
            term_text = str(term).strip()
            if not term_text:
                continue

            term_lower = term_text.lower()

            if term_lower in haystack_lower:
                matched.append(term_text)

                # Base occurrence score.
                score += max(1, haystack_lower.count(term_lower))

                # Useful boosts for ATLAS-style retrieval.
                if term_lower == id_lower:
                    score += 12.0
                elif term_lower in id_lower:
                    score += 6.0

                if term_lower == name_lower:
                    score += 10.0
                elif term_lower in name_lower:
                    score += 4.0

                if term_lower == entity_lower:
                    score += 2.0

                if term_text.startswith("#"):
                    score += 5.0

        operator = str(operator or "any").strip().lower()

        if operator == "all" and len(matched) < len(keywords):
            return 0.0, matched

        # Small bonus when the whole query appears as a phrase.
        query_lower = str(query).strip().lower()
        if query_lower and query_lower in haystack_lower:
            score += 5.0

        return score, matched

    def _safe_list(self, value: Any) -> Any:
        if value is None:
            return []

        if isinstance(value, list):
            return value

        if isinstance(value, str):
            text = value.strip()
            if text == "":
                return []

            try:
                parsed = ast.literal_eval(text)
                if isinstance(parsed, list):
                    return parsed
            except Exception:
                pass

        return value

    def _query_semantic(
        self,
        collection,
        query: str,
        n_results: int,
        where: dict | None,
    ) -> list[dict]:
        kwargs = {
            "query_texts": [query],
            "n_results": n_results,
            "include": ["documents", "metadatas", "distances"],
        }

        if where:
            kwargs["where"] = where

        results = collection.query(**kwargs)

        ids = results.get("ids", [[]])[0] or []
        docs = results.get("documents", [[]])[0] or []
        metas = results.get("metadatas", [[]])[0] or []
        distances = results.get("distances", [[]])[0] or []

        items = []

        for idx, chroma_id in enumerate(ids):
            metadata = metas[idx] if idx < len(metas) and metas[idx] else {}
            document = docs[idx] if idx < len(docs) else ""
            distance = distances[idx] if idx < len(distances) else None

            items.append(
                {
                    "query": query,
                    "chroma_id": chroma_id,
                    "document": document,
                    "metadata": metadata,
                    "semantic_rank": idx + 1,
                    "semantic_distance": distance,
                    "keyword_rank": None,
                    "keyword_score": 0.0,
                    "matched_keywords": [],
                }
            )

        return items

    def _get_keyword_candidates(
        self,
        collection,
        query: str,
        keywords: list[str],
        where: dict | None,
        keyword_operator: str,
        max_keyword_scan: int,
    ) -> list[dict]:
        if not keywords:
            return []

        count = collection.count()

        if count <= 0:
            return []

        # For small collections, scan locally so matching is case-insensitive
        # and can include metadata fields, not only Chroma document text.
        if count <= max_keyword_scan:
            kwargs = {
                "include": ["documents", "metadatas"],
                "limit": count,
            }

            if where:
                kwargs["where"] = where

            results = collection.get(**kwargs)

        else:
            # For larger collections, use Chroma where_document as a coarse
            # prefilter. Note: Chroma full-text contains matching is case-sensitive.
            where_document = self._build_where_document(keywords, keyword_operator)

            kwargs = {
                "include": ["documents", "metadatas"],
                "limit": max_keyword_scan,
            }

            if where:
                kwargs["where"] = where

            if where_document:
                kwargs["where_document"] = where_document

            results = collection.get(**kwargs)

        ids = results.get("ids", []) or []
        docs = results.get("documents", []) or []
        metas = results.get("metadatas", []) or []

        scored = []

        for idx, chroma_id in enumerate(ids):
            metadata = metas[idx] if idx < len(metas) and metas[idx] else {}
            document = docs[idx] if idx < len(docs) else ""

            score, matched = self._keyword_score(
                query=query,
                document=document,
                metadata=metadata,
                keywords=keywords,
                operator=keyword_operator,
            )

            if score <= 0:
                continue

            scored.append(
                {
                    "query": query,
                    "chroma_id": chroma_id,
                    "document": document,
                    "metadata": metadata,
                    "semantic_rank": None,
                    "semantic_distance": None,
                    "keyword_rank": None,
                    "keyword_score": score,
                    "matched_keywords": matched,
                }
            )

        scored.sort(key=lambda item: item["keyword_score"], reverse=True)

        for idx, item in enumerate(scored):
            item["keyword_rank"] = idx + 1

        return scored

    def _dedupe_key(self, item: dict, dedupe_by: str) -> str:
        metadata = item.get("metadata") or {}

        if dedupe_by == "id":
            atlas_id = metadata.get("id")
            if atlas_id:
                return str(atlas_id)

        return str(item.get("chroma_id", ""))

    def _fuse_results(
        self,
        semantic_items: list[dict],
        keyword_items: list[dict],
        n_results: int,
        semantic_weight: float,
        keyword_weight: float,
        dedupe_by: str,
    ) -> list[dict]:
        rrf_k = 60.0
        buckets = {}

        for item in semantic_items:
            key = self._dedupe_key(item, dedupe_by)
            if not key:
                continue

            current = buckets.setdefault(key, item.copy())

            if current.get("semantic_rank") is None:
                current["semantic_rank"] = item.get("semantic_rank")
                current["semantic_distance"] = item.get("semantic_distance")
            elif item.get("semantic_rank") is not None:
                if item["semantic_rank"] < current["semantic_rank"]:
                    current["semantic_rank"] = item["semantic_rank"]
                    current["semantic_distance"] = item.get("semantic_distance")

        for item in keyword_items:
            key = self._dedupe_key(item, dedupe_by)
            if not key:
                continue

            current = buckets.setdefault(key, item.copy())

            if current.get("keyword_rank") is None:
                current["keyword_rank"] = item.get("keyword_rank")
                current["keyword_score"] = item.get("keyword_score", 0.0)
                current["matched_keywords"] = item.get("matched_keywords", [])
            elif item.get("keyword_rank") is not None:
                if item["keyword_rank"] < current["keyword_rank"]:
                    current["keyword_rank"] = item["keyword_rank"]
                    current["keyword_score"] = item.get("keyword_score", 0.0)
                    current["matched_keywords"] = item.get("matched_keywords", [])

        fused = []

        for item in buckets.values():
            semantic_rank = item.get("semantic_rank")
            keyword_rank = item.get("keyword_rank")

            semantic_rrf = 0.0
            keyword_rrf = 0.0

            if semantic_rank is not None:
                semantic_rrf = 1.0 / (rrf_k + float(semantic_rank))

            if keyword_rank is not None:
                keyword_rrf = 1.0 / (rrf_k + float(keyword_rank))

            hybrid_score = (
                semantic_weight * semantic_rrf
                + keyword_weight * keyword_rrf
            )

            # Small direct keyword score boost.
            hybrid_score += min(float(item.get("keyword_score", 0.0)), 20.0) / 1000.0

            item["hybrid_score"] = hybrid_score
            fused.append(item)

        fused.sort(key=lambda item: item.get("hybrid_score", 0.0), reverse=True)

        return fused[:n_results]

    def _items_to_rows(self, items: list[dict], mode: str) -> list[dict]:
        rows = []

        for rank, item in enumerate(items, start=1):
            metadata = item.get("metadata") or {}

            row = {
                "query": item.get("query", ""),
                "rank": rank,
                "search_mode": mode,
                "hybrid_score": item.get("hybrid_score"),
                "semantic_rank": item.get("semantic_rank"),
                "semantic_distance": item.get("semantic_distance"),
                "keyword_rank": item.get("keyword_rank"),
                "keyword_score": item.get("keyword_score"),
                "matched_keywords": item.get("matched_keywords", []),
                "chroma_id": item.get("chroma_id", ""),
                "id": metadata.get("id", ""),
                "text": item.get("document", ""),
                "entity": metadata.get("entity", ""),
                "name": metadata.get("name", ""),
                "description": metadata.get("description", ""),
                "url": metadata.get("url", ""),
                "framework": metadata.get("framework", ""),
                "hashtags": self._safe_list(metadata.get("hashtags")),
                "hashtags_text": metadata.get("hashtags_text", ""),
                "PARENT_TACTICS": self._safe_list(metadata.get("PARENT_TACTICS")),
                "PARENT_TECHNIQUES": self._safe_list(metadata.get("PARENT_TECHNIQUES")),
                "PARENT_MITIGATIONS": self._safe_list(metadata.get("PARENT_MITIGATIONS")),
                "PARENT_CASESTUDIES": self._safe_list(metadata.get("PARENT_CASESTUDIES")),
                "CHILD_TECHNIQUES": self._safe_list(metadata.get("CHILD_TECHNIQUES")),
            }

            rows.append(row)

        return rows

    def build_output(self) -> DataFrame:
        query_texts = [q.strip() for q in str(self.queries or "").split("\n") if q.strip()]

        if not query_texts:
            return DataFrame([])

        search_mode = str(self.search_mode or "hybrid").strip().lower()
        if search_mode not in {"semantic", "keyword", "hybrid", "tag_filtered_semantic"}:
            search_mode = "hybrid"

        keyword_operator = str(self.keyword_operator or "any").strip().lower()
        if keyword_operator not in {"any", "all"}:
            keyword_operator = "any"

        hashtag_operator = str(self.hashtag_operator or "any").strip().lower()
        if hashtag_operator not in {"any", "all"}:
            hashtag_operator = "any"

        semantic_weight = self._parse_float(self.semantic_weight, 0.65)
        keyword_weight = self._parse_float(self.keyword_weight, 0.35)

        if semantic_weight < 0:
            semantic_weight = 0.0

        if keyword_weight < 0:
            keyword_weight = 0.0

        total_weight = semantic_weight + keyword_weight
        if total_weight <= 0:
            semantic_weight = 0.65
            keyword_weight = 0.35
        else:
            semantic_weight = semantic_weight / total_weight
            keyword_weight = keyword_weight / total_weight

        n_results = int(self.n_results or 5)
        candidate_pool = max(int(self.candidate_pool or 25), n_results)
        max_keyword_scan = int(self.max_keyword_scan or 5000)

        explicit_keywords = self._parse_lines(self.keyword_terms)
        hashtags = self._parse_lines(self.hashtags)

        metadata_where = self._parse_where(self.metadata_where)
        hashtag_where = self._build_hashtag_where(hashtags, hashtag_operator)
        where = self._merge_where(metadata_where, hashtag_where)

        persist_path = Path(self.persistence_path)
        persist_path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

        chroma_client = chromadb.PersistentClient(path=str(persist_path))
        collection = chroma_client.get_collection(name=self.collection_name)

        rows = []

        for query in query_texts:
            query_keywords = explicit_keywords or self._derive_keywords(query)

            semantic_items = []
            keyword_items = []

            if search_mode in {"semantic", "hybrid", "tag_filtered_semantic"}:
                semantic_items = self._query_semantic(
                    collection=collection,
                    query=query,
                    n_results=candidate_pool,
                    where=where,
                )

            if search_mode in {"keyword", "hybrid"}:
                keyword_items = self._get_keyword_candidates(
                    collection=collection,
                    query=query,
                    keywords=query_keywords,
                    where=where,
                    keyword_operator=keyword_operator,
                    max_keyword_scan=max_keyword_scan,
                )

            if search_mode == "semantic" or search_mode == "tag_filtered_semantic":
                selected = semantic_items[:n_results]
                for item in selected:
                    item["hybrid_score"] = None

            elif search_mode == "keyword":
                selected = keyword_items[:n_results]
                for item in selected:
                    item["hybrid_score"] = item.get("keyword_score", 0.0)

            else:
                selected = self._fuse_results(
                    semantic_items=semantic_items,
                    keyword_items=keyword_items,
                    n_results=n_results,
                    semantic_weight=semantic_weight,
                    keyword_weight=keyword_weight,
                    dedupe_by=str(self.dedupe_by or "chroma_id").strip().lower(),
                )

            rows.extend(self._items_to_rows(selected, search_mode))

        return DataFrame(rows)

    def _resolve_selected_model(self):
        """Resolve the selected model, including legacy agent_llm/model_name inputs."""
        try:
            from langchain_core.language_models import BaseLanguageModel

            if isinstance(self.model, BaseLanguageModel):
                return self.model
        except ImportError:
            pass

        if isinstance(self.model, list) and self.model:
            return self.model

        legacy_provider = getattr(self, "agent_llm", None)
        legacy_model_name = getattr(self, "model_name", None)
        if not legacy_provider or not legacy_model_name:
            return self.model

        options = get_language_model_options(user_id=self.user_id)
        for option in options:
            if option.get("provider") == legacy_provider and option.get("name") == legacy_model_name:
                return [option]

        return [
            {
                "name": legacy_model_name,
                "provider": legacy_provider,
                "metadata": {},
            }
        ]

    def _get_max_tokens_value(self):
        """Return the user-supplied max_tokens or None when unset/zero."""
        val = getattr(self, "max_tokens", None)
        if val in {"", 0}:
            return None
        return val

    def _get_llm(self):
        """Override parent to include max_tokens from the Agent's input field."""
        return get_llm(
            model=self.model,
            user_id=self.user_id,
            api_key=getattr(self, "api_key", None),
            max_tokens=self._get_max_tokens_value(),
            watsonx_url=getattr(self, "base_url_ibm_watsonx", None),
            watsonx_project_id=getattr(self, "project_id", None),
        )

    async def get_agent_requirements(self):
        """Get the agent requirements for the agent."""
        from langchain_core.tools import StructuredTool

        selected_model = self._resolve_selected_model()
        try:
            from langchain_core.language_models import BaseLanguageModel

            is_connected_model = isinstance(selected_model, BaseLanguageModel)
        except ImportError:
            is_connected_model = False

        if not is_connected_model:
            validate_model_selection(selected_model)

        # Ensure _get_llm() uses the resolved model (e.g. from legacy agent_llm/model_name)
        self.model = selected_model
        llm_model = self._get_llm()
        if llm_model is None:
            msg = "No language model selected. Please choose a model to proceed."
            raise ValueError(msg)

        # Get memory data
        self.chat_history = await self.get_memory_data()
        await logger.adebug(f"Retrieved {len(self.chat_history)} chat history messages")
        if isinstance(self.chat_history, Message):
            self.chat_history = [self.chat_history]

        # Add current date tool if enabled
        if self.add_current_date_tool:
            if not isinstance(self.tools, list):  # type: ignore[has-type]
                self.tools = []
            current_date_tool = (await CurrentDateComponent(**self.get_base_args()).to_toolkit()).pop(0)

            if not isinstance(current_date_tool, StructuredTool):
                msg = "CurrentDateComponent must be converted to a StructuredTool"
                raise TypeError(msg)
            self.tools.append(current_date_tool)

        # Set shared callbacks for tracing the tools used by the agent
        self.set_tools_callbacks(self.tools, self._get_shared_callbacks())

        return llm_model, self.chat_history, self.tools

    async def message_response(self) -> Message:
        try:
            llm_model, self.chat_history, self.tools = await self.get_agent_requirements()
            # Set up and run agent
            self.set(
                llm=llm_model,
                tools=self.tools or [],
                chat_history=self.chat_history,
                input_value=self.input_value,
                system_prompt=self.system_prompt,
            )
            agent = self.create_agent_runnable()
            result = await self.run_agent(agent)

            # Store result for potential JSON output
            self._agent_result = result

        except (ValueError, TypeError, KeyError) as e:
            await logger.aerror(f"{type(e).__name__}: {e!s}")
            raise
        except ExceptionWithMessageError as e:
            await logger.aerror(f"ExceptionWithMessageError occurred: {e}")
            raise
        # Avoid catching blind Exception; let truly unexpected exceptions propagate
        except Exception as e:
            await logger.aerror(f"Unexpected error: {e!s}")
            raise
        else:
            return result

    def _preprocess_schema(self, schema):
        """Preprocess schema to ensure correct data types for build_model_from_schema."""
        processed_schema = []
        for field in schema:
            processed_field = {
                "name": str(field.get("name", "field")),
                "type": str(field.get("type", "str")),
                "description": str(field.get("description", "")),
                "multiple": field.get("multiple", False),
            }
            # Ensure multiple is handled correctly
            if isinstance(processed_field["multiple"], str):
                processed_field["multiple"] = processed_field["multiple"].lower() in [
                    "true",
                    "1",
                    "t",
                    "y",
                    "yes",
                ]
            processed_schema.append(processed_field)
        return processed_schema

    async def json_response(self) -> Data:
        """Convert agent response to structured JSON Data output with schema validation."""
        # Always use structured chat agent for JSON response mode for better JSON formatting
        try:
            system_components = []

            # 1. Agent Instructions (system_prompt)
            agent_instructions = getattr(self, "system_prompt", "") or ""
            if agent_instructions:
                system_components.append(f"{agent_instructions}")

            # 2. Format Instructions
            format_instructions = getattr(self, "format_instructions", "") or ""
            if format_instructions:
                system_components.append(f"Format instructions: {format_instructions}")

            # 3. Schema Information from BaseModel
            if hasattr(self, "output_schema") and self.output_schema and len(self.output_schema) > 0:
                try:
                    processed_schema = self._preprocess_schema(self.output_schema)
                    output_model = build_model_from_schema(processed_schema)
                    schema_dict = output_model.model_json_schema()
                    schema_info = (
                        "You are given some text that may include format instructions, "
                        "explanations, or other content alongside a JSON schema.\n\n"
                        "Your task:\n"
                        "- Extract only the JSON schema.\n"
                        "- Return it as valid JSON.\n"
                        "- Do not include format instructions, explanations, or extra text.\n\n"
                        "Input:\n"
                        f"{json.dumps(schema_dict, indent=2)}\n\n"
                        "Output (only JSON schema):"
                    )
                    system_components.append(schema_info)
                except (ValidationError, ValueError, TypeError, KeyError) as e:
                    await logger.aerror(f"Could not build schema for prompt: {e}", exc_info=True)

            # Combine all components
            combined_instructions = "\n\n".join(system_components) if system_components else ""
            llm_model, self.chat_history, self.tools = await self.get_agent_requirements()
            self.set(
                llm=llm_model,
                tools=self.tools or [],
                chat_history=self.chat_history,
                input_value=self.input_value,
                system_prompt=combined_instructions,
            )

            # Create and run structured chat agent
            try:
                structured_agent = self.create_agent_runnable()
            except (NotImplementedError, ValueError, TypeError) as e:
                await logger.aerror(f"Error with structured chat agent: {e}")
                raise
            try:
                result = await self.run_agent(structured_agent)
            except (
                ExceptionWithMessageError,
                ValueError,
                TypeError,
                RuntimeError,
            ) as e:
                await logger.aerror(f"Error with structured agent result: {e}")
                raise
            # Extract content from structured agent result
            if hasattr(result, "content"):
                content = result.content
            elif hasattr(result, "text"):
                content = result.text
            else:
                content = str(result)

        except (
            ExceptionWithMessageError,
            ValueError,
            TypeError,
            NotImplementedError,
            AttributeError,
        ) as e:
            await logger.aerror(f"Error with structured chat agent: {e}")
            # Fallback to regular agent
            content_str = "No content returned from agent"
            return Data(data={"content": content_str, "error": str(e)})

        # Process with structured output validation
        try:
            structured_output = await self.build_structured_output_base(content)

            # Handle different output formats
            if isinstance(structured_output, list) and structured_output:
                if len(structured_output) == 1:
                    return Data(data=structured_output[0])
                return Data(data={"results": structured_output})
            if isinstance(structured_output, dict):
                return Data(data=structured_output)
            return Data(data={"content": content})

        except (ValueError, TypeError) as e:
            await logger.aerror(f"Error in structured output processing: {e}")
            return Data(data={"content": content, "error": str(e)})

    def update_input_types(self, build_config: dotdict) -> dotdict:
        """Update input types for all fields in build_config."""
        for key, value in build_config.items():
            if isinstance(value, dict):
                if value.get("input_types") is None:
                    build_config[key]["input_types"] = []
            elif hasattr(value, "input_types") and value.input_types is None:
                value.input_types = []
        return build_config

    async def update_build_config(
        self,
        build_config: dotdict,
        field_value: list[dict],
        field_name: str | None = None,
    ) -> dotdict:
        # Update model options with caching (for all field changes)
        # Agents require tool calling, so filter for only tool-calling capable models
        build_config = handle_model_input_update(
            component=self,
            build_config=dict(build_config),
            field_value=field_value,
            field_name=field_name,
            cache_key_prefix="language_model_options_tool_calling",
            get_options_func=lambda user_id=None: get_language_model_options(user_id=user_id, tool_calling=True),
        )
        build_config = dotdict(build_config)

        if field_name == "model":
            build_config = self.update_input_types(build_config)

            # Validate required keys
            default_keys = [
                "code",
                "_type",
                "model",
                "tools",
                "input_value",
                "add_current_date_tool",
                "system_prompt",
                "agent_description",
                "max_iterations",
                "handle_parsing_errors",
                "verbose",
            ]
            missing_keys = [key for key in default_keys if key not in build_config]
            if missing_keys:
                msg = f"Missing required keys in build_config: {missing_keys}"
                raise ValueError(msg)
        return dotdict({k: v.to_dict() if hasattr(v, "to_dict") else v for k, v in build_config.items()})

    async def _get_tools(self) -> list[Tool]:
        component_toolkit = get_component_toolkit()
        tools_names = self._build_tools_names()
        agent_description = self.get_tool_description()
        # TODO: Agent Description Depreciated Feature to be removed
        description = f"{agent_description}{tools_names}"

        tools = component_toolkit(component=self).get_tools(
            tool_name="Call_Agent",
            tool_description=description,
            # here we do not use the shared callbacks as we are exposing the agent as a tool
            callbacks=self.get_langchain_callbacks(),
        )
        if hasattr(self, "tools_metadata"):
            tools = component_toolkit(component=self, metadata=self.tools_metadata).update_tools_metadata(tools=tools)

        return tools

system_prompt.value:
You are the ATLAS Vector Store Agent.

Your sole purpose is to perform semantic similarity search over the ATLAS Knowledge Base using the provided semantic search tool.

You receive a text query from the Orchestrator. The query may describe:
- An ATLAS entity name
- A partial or approximate ATLAS entity name
- A partial or approximate entity description
- A threat scenario
- A defense concept
- A mitigation goal
- A case-study-like scenario
- A user’s natural-language description of adversarial behavior against AI systems

Do not produce the final user-facing answer.

Return semantically relevant ATLAS entity candidates for the Orchestrator to verify, hydrate, rank, and synthesize.

Your output must use the same top-level structure as the Dataset Agent response schema so the Orchestrator can process both agents consistently.

---

# Core Responsibility

You are responsible for semantic retrieval only.

You may:
- Search for ATLAS entities that are semantically similar to the query.
- Return multiple candidate entities when the query is broad, vague, or underspecified.
- Identify approximate matches to entity names or descriptions.
- Surface potentially relevant tactics, techniques, mitigations, and case studies.
- Provide short evidence-based rationales in `notes`.
- Note ambiguity or alternate interpretations in `notes`.

You must not:
- Produce the final answer to the user.
- Perform exact dataset hydration.
- Perform authoritative ID lookup.
- Perform relationship traversal.
- Count, aggregate, sort, or analyze the full dataset.
- Infer relationships that are not explicitly present in retrieved chunks.
- Invent ATLAS IDs, names, URLs, descriptions, or relationships.
- Treat semantic matches as verified facts.
- Claim that a candidate is definitive unless the retrieved text strongly supports it.

The Dataset Agent is responsible for exact lookup, hydration, filtering, counting, relationship traversal, and dataset-grounded verification.

---

# Tool

## `SEMANTIC_SEARCH`

Use `SEMANTIC_SEARCH` for all semantic retrieval tasks.

`SEMANTIC_SEARCH` performs semantic similarity search over ATLAS Knowledge Base entries.

Each retrieved result may represent one ATLAS entity:
- `tactic`
- `technique`
- `mitigation`
- `casestudy`

Each retrieved context chunk may contain:
- `id`
- `entity`
- `name`
- `text`
- `url`
- `PARENT_TACTICS`
- `PARENT_TECHNIQUES`
- `PARENT_MITIGATIONS`
- `PARENT_CASESTUDIES`
- `CHILD_TECHNIQUES`

Use `SEMANTIC_SEARCH` when the Orchestrator asks for:
- Relevant ATLAS entries for a natural-language scenario
- Techniques related to a behavior or attack pattern
- Mitigations related to a defense goal
- Tactics, techniques, mitigations, or case studies matching an approximate description
- Candidate IDs for later dataset hydration
- Broad discovery over the ATLAS knowledge base
- Similarity search against user-provided text

---

# Tool Use Rules

Always use `SEMANTIC_SEARCH` when responding to a semantic retrieval request.

Use the Orchestrator’s instruction as the search query, but rewrite internally only when it improves retrieval clarity. Preserve the original query meaning in the returned `notes` when relevant.

When the query is short, vague, or ambiguous:
- Prefer recall over precision.
- Return multiple plausible candidates.
- Explain ambiguity in `notes`.
- Include weaker candidates only when useful.

When the query is specific:
- Prefer precision.
- Return the strongest matches first.
- Avoid padding with weakly related candidates unless the Orchestrator requested broad recall.

When the query appears to request exact dataset operations, do not attempt to answer them semantically. Return a routing-style structured response using the shared schema.

---

# Supported Query Types

You can perform semantic retrieval for queries such as:

- “Find ATLAS techniques related to prompt injection.”
- “What ATLAS entries are relevant to an attacker manipulating model outputs?”
- “Find mitigations for training data poisoning.”
- “Which ATLAS techniques resemble model evasion?”
- “Find case studies involving adversarial examples.”
- “What ATLAS concepts apply to stealing a model?”
- “Find entries related to exfiltrating sensitive data from an AI system.”
- “Find techniques where an attacker causes the model to behave incorrectly.”
- “Find mitigations related to monitoring model behavior.”
- “Find ATLAS entries relevant to this scenario: [scenario text].”

---

# Retrieval Strategy

Use the user’s scenario or description to retrieve semantically similar ATLAS entities.

When useful, emphasize these semantic dimensions:
- Adversarial behavior
- Targeted AI lifecycle phase
- Attack objective
- Attack mechanism
- Defensive control or mitigation goal
- Observable behavior
- Impact on model, data, system, or user
- Similarity to known ATLAS tactic, technique, mitigation, or case study descriptions

Do not rely on general cybersecurity assumptions unless they are reflected in retrieved ATLAS text.

Do not expand the scope beyond the query unless the Orchestrator explicitly asks for broad discovery.

---

# Ranking Guidance

Rank records by semantic relevance to the query.

Prefer higher ranking for records where:
- The retrieved `name` closely matches the query.
- The retrieved `text` directly describes the behavior, defense, or scenario.
- The retrieved entity type matches the requested type, if specified.
- Multiple parts of the retrieved record support the match.
- The match is specific rather than merely adjacent.

Lower ranking for records where:
- The match is based on broad topical overlap only.
- The entity is related to the general domain but not the specific behavior.
- The retrieved text supports only part of the query.
- The match depends on unstated assumptions.

Because the shared response schema does not include a dedicated `match_confidence` field, include confidence and rationale in `notes` rather than adding non-schema fields to each record.

---

# Match Confidence Guidance

Use `notes` to communicate confidence when useful.

Use `high confidence` when:
- The query directly matches the entity name, or
- The retrieved text clearly and specifically describes the requested behavior, defense, or scenario, or
- The requested entity type and the retrieved entity type align exactly.

Use `medium confidence` when:
- The retrieved entity is plausibly relevant, but the match is indirect.
- The result matches part of the query but not all of it.
- The relationship to the query is clear but somewhat general.
- The entity type is relevant but not explicitly requested.

Use `low confidence` when:
- The result is only broadly related.
- The query is vague and the candidate is one possible interpretation.
- The retrieved text has weak or partial overlap.
- The candidate may be useful for exploration but needs verification.

Do not use high-confidence language when the match depends on inference beyond retrieved text.

---

# Entity Type Handling

If the Orchestrator requests a specific entity type, such as techniques or mitigations:
- Prefer records of that entity type.
- Exclude unrelated entity types unless they are highly relevant and useful to the Orchestrator.
- Note when returned records include other entity types.

If the Orchestrator does not specify an entity type:
- Return the most semantically relevant mix of tactics, techniques, mitigations, and case studies.
- Do not force diversity if one entity type clearly dominates the relevant results.

Use `casestudy` exactly as the entity value for case studies.

---

# Relationship Handling

Retrieved chunks may include relationship fields.

You may report relationships only when they are explicitly present in the retrieved chunk:
- `PARENT_TACTICS`
- `PARENT_TECHNIQUES`
- `PARENT_MITIGATIONS`
- `PARENT_CASESTUDIES`
- `CHILD_TECHNIQUES`

Do not:
- Infer missing relationships.
- Traverse relationships.
- Hydrate related IDs.
- Claim that a relationship exists unless it appears in the retrieved result.
- Use relationships to answer structured graph questions.

If the Orchestrator needs relationship traversal or hydrated relationship details, note that the Dataset Agent or Graph Agent should handle that next.

---

# Handling Exact-ID Queries

If the query consists primarily of exact AML.IDs or asks to hydrate known IDs, semantic search is not appropriate.

Return:

```json
{
  "status": "needs_dataset_lookup",
  "operation": "routing_note",
  "tool_used": null,
  "records": [],
  "notes": [
    "This is an exact AML.ID lookup or hydration request. The Dataset Agent should handle it using ID_LOOKUP."
  ]
}
````

If the query includes both exact IDs and semantic context:

* Use semantic search only for the natural-language portion if useful.
* Include a note that exact IDs should be hydrated by the Dataset Agent.
* Do not claim retrieved records are authoritative replacements for ID lookup.

---

# Handling Structured Dataset Queries

If the query asks for counts, filters, lists, field selection, aggregations, or relationship traversal, semantic search is not appropriate.

Return:

```json
{
  "status": "needs_dataset_analysis",
  "operation": "routing_note",
  "tool_used": null,
  "records": [],
  "notes": [
    "This is a structured dataset query. The Dataset Agent should handle it using PANDAS_EXPERT or ID_LOOKUP."
  ]
}
```

Examples:

* “How many techniques are there?”
* “List all mitigations.”
* “Which techniques have mitigations?”
* “Return the URLs for all case studies.”
* “What are the children of AML.M0003?”
* “Which tactics have more than 10 child techniques?”

---

# Handling Graph Queries

If the query asks for graph structure, paths, neighborhoods, connected components, relationship chains, visualization, Kumu URL, or multi-hop traversal, semantic search is not appropriate unless the Orchestrator explicitly asks for candidate entities first.

Return:

```json
{
  "status": "needs_graph_analysis",
  "operation": "routing_note",
  "tool_used": null,
  "records": [],
  "notes": [
    "This is a graph-structured or visualization query. The Graph Agent should handle relationship traversal, graph analysis, or Kumu URL generation after IDs are verified."
  ]
}
```

Examples:

* “Show all paths from this tactic to its mitigations.”
* “What is connected to AML.T0001 within two hops?”
* “Find clusters of related techniques.”
* “Which mitigations connect the most techniques?”
* “Find the shortest path between these entities.”
* “Generate a Kumu graph for this scenario.”

---

# Output Format

Return JSON-compatible structured output using the same top-level response structure as the Dataset Agent.

Do not use `results`, `candidate_ids`, `relationships_observed`, `summary`, or `match_confidence` as top-level or per-record fields.

Place retrieved candidate entities in `records`.

Place match rationales, confidence, ambiguity, and routing guidance in `notes`.

---

## Successful semantic retrieval response

```json
{
  "status": "success",
  "operation": "semantic_search",
  "tool_used": "SEMANTIC_SEARCH",
  "records": [
    {
      "id": "AML...",
      "entity": "tactic | technique | mitigation | casestudy",
      "name": "Entity name",
      "text": "Retrieved ATLAS description or context text.",
      "url": "URL if available",
      "PARENT_TACTICS": [],
      "PARENT_TECHNIQUES": [],
      "PARENT_MITIGATIONS": [],
      "PARENT_CASESTUDIES": [],
      "CHILD_TECHNIQUES": []
    }
  ],
  "notes": [
    "Semantic candidate retrieval only. Records should be verified or hydrated by the Dataset Agent before final use.",
    "AML...: high confidence because the retrieved text directly matches the scenario."
  ]
}
```

---

## Weak or ambiguous semantic retrieval response

Use this when there are plausible semantic candidates but the query is broad, vague, or the matches are only partial.

```json
{
  "status": "partial_match",
  "operation": "semantic_search",
  "tool_used": "SEMANTIC_SEARCH",
  "records": [
    {
      "id": "AML...",
      "entity": "tactic | technique | mitigation | casestudy",
      "name": "Entity name",
      "text": "Retrieved ATLAS description or context text.",
      "url": "URL if available",
      "PARENT_TACTICS": [],
      "PARENT_TECHNIQUES": [],
      "PARENT_MITIGATIONS": [],
      "PARENT_CASESTUDIES": [],
      "CHILD_TECHNIQUES": []
    }
  ],
  "notes": [
    "The query is broad or ambiguous. These are candidate semantic matches, not verified final answers.",
    "AML...: medium confidence because the retrieved text partially overlaps with the query.",
    "The Dataset Agent should hydrate and verify selected candidate IDs before final synthesis."
  ]
}
```

---

## No useful semantic matches response

Use this only when the semantic search returns no usable candidates.

```json
{
  "status": "no_match",
  "operation": "semantic_search",
  "tool_used": "SEMANTIC_SEARCH",
  "records": [],
  "notes": [
    "No useful semantic matches were found in the retrieved ATLAS context."
  ]
}
```

---

## Needs dataset lookup response

```json
{
  "status": "needs_dataset_lookup",
  "operation": "routing_note",
  "tool_used": null,
  "records": [],
  "notes": [
    "This is an exact AML.ID lookup or hydration request. The Dataset Agent should handle it."
  ]
}
```

---

## Needs dataset analysis response

```json
{
  "status": "needs_dataset_analysis",
  "operation": "routing_note",
  "tool_used": null,
  "records": [],
  "notes": [
    "This is a structured dataset query. The Dataset Agent should handle filtering, counting, aggregation, or relationship lookup."
  ]
}
```

---

## Needs graph analysis response

```json
{
  "status": "needs_graph_analysis",
  "operation": "routing_note",
  "tool_used": null,
  "records": [],
  "notes": [
    "This is a graph-structured or visualization query. The Graph Agent should handle relationship traversal, graph analysis, or Kumu URL generation."
  ]
}
```

---

# Record Construction Rules

For each retrieved record:

* Preserve the retrieved `id` exactly.
* Preserve the retrieved `entity` exactly, except use `casestudy` consistently for case studies.
* Preserve the retrieved `name` exactly.
* Include retrieved `text` exactly or as the most relevant available retrieved description/context.
* Include the retrieved `url` if available.
* Include relationship fields only when explicitly present in the retrieved chunk.
* Use empty arrays for missing relationship fields.
* Do not include fields outside the shared record schema.

Required record fields:

```json
{
  "id": "...",
  "entity": "...",
  "name": "...",
  "text": "...",
  "url": "...",
  "PARENT_TACTICS": [],
  "PARENT_TECHNIQUES": [],
  "PARENT_MITIGATIONS": [],
  "PARENT_CASESTUDIES": [],
  "CHILD_TECHNIQUES": []
}
```

Do not include duplicate IDs in `records`.

If multiple chunks refer to the same entity:

* Merge them into one record.
* Keep the clearest and most relevant text available.
* Preserve observed relationships without inventing missing ones.
* Add a note if multiple chunks supported the same candidate.

---

# Notes Guidance

Use `notes` to tell the Orchestrator:

* That returned records are semantic candidates.
* Whether the query was ambiguous.
* Whether matches are high, medium, or low confidence.
* Why each important candidate matched the query.
* Whether exact hydration should be performed by the Dataset Agent.
* Whether relationship traversal should be performed by the Graph Agent or Dataset Agent.
* Whether the search was constrained by retrieved context.

Keep notes concise and operational.

Preferred note format for candidate rationales:

```text
AML.T####: high confidence — retrieved text directly describes [brief reason].
AML.T####: medium confidence — overlaps with [brief reason], but does not cover [missing aspect].
AML.T####: low confidence — broad topical overlap only.
```

---

# Constraints

* Always ground records in retrieved vector-store content.
* Do not invent ATLAS IDs.
* Do not invent entity names.
* Do not invent text, URLs, or relationships.
* Do not infer missing relationships.
* Do not hydrate related IDs.
* Do not count, aggregate, or analyze the full dataset.
* Do not perform graph traversal.
* Do not provide final user-facing synthesis.
* Treat semantic results as candidates, not authoritative final answers.
* Prefer recall over precision for broad or ambiguous queries.
* Prefer precision over recall for specific queries.
* If no strong matches are found, return the closest weak matches when useful.
* Use `casestudy` consistently as the entity value.

from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI
from pydantic.v1 import SecretStr

from lfx.base.models.model import LCModelComponent
from lfx.base.models.openai_constants import OPENAI_CHAT_MODEL_NAMES, OPENAI_REASONING_MODEL_NAMES

from lfx.inputs.inputs import BoolInput, DictInput, DropdownInput, IntInput, SecretStrInput, SliderInput, StrInput
from lfx.log.logger import logger


class OpenAIModelComponent(LCModelComponent):
    display_name = "AIP LLM"
    description = "Generates text using AIP LLMs."
    icon = "OpenAI"
    name = "OpenAIModel"

    inputs = [
        *LCModelComponent.get_base_inputs(),
        IntInput(
            name="max_tokens",
            display_name="Max Tokens",
            advanced=True,
            info="The maximum number of tokens to generate. Set to 0 for unlimited tokens.",
            range_spec=RangeSpec(min=0, max=128000),
        ),
        DictInput(
            name="model_kwargs",
            display_name="Model Kwargs",
            advanced=True,
            info="Additional keyword arguments to pass to the model.",
        ),
        BoolInput(
            name="json_mode",
            display_name="JSON Mode",
            advanced=True,
            info="If True, it will output JSON regardless of passing a schema.",
        ),
        StrInput(
            name="model_name",
            display_name="Model Name",
            advanced=True,
        ),
        StrInput(
            name="openai_api_base",
            display_name="OpenAI API Base",
            advanced=True,
            info="The base URL of the OpenAI API. "
            "Defaults to https://api.openai.com/v1. "
            "You can change this to use other APIs like JinaChat, LocalAI and Prem.",
        ),
        SecretStrInput(
            name="api_key",
            display_name="OpenAI API Key",
            info="The OpenAI API Key to use for the OpenAI model.",
            advanced=False,
            value="OPENAI_API_KEY",
            required=True,
        ),
        SliderInput(
            name="temperature",
            display_name="Temperature",
            value=0.1,
            range_spec=RangeSpec(min=0, max=1, step=0.01),
            show=True,
        ),
        IntInput(
            name="seed",
            display_name="Seed",
            info="The seed controls the reproducibility of the job.",
            advanced=True,
            value=1,
        ),
        IntInput(
            name="max_retries",
            display_name="Max Retries",
            info="The maximum number of retries to make when generating.",
            advanced=True,
            value=5,
        ),
        IntInput(
            name="timeout",
            display_name="Timeout",
            info="The timeout for requests to OpenAI completion API.",
            advanced=True,
            value=700,
        ),
    ]

    def build_model(self) -> LanguageModel:  # type: ignore[type-var]
        logger.debug(f"Executing request with model: {self.model_name}")
        # Handle api_key - it can be string or SecretStr
        api_key_value = None
        if self.api_key:
            logger.debug(f"API key type: {type(self.api_key)}, value: {'***' if self.api_key else None}")
            if isinstance(self.api_key, SecretStr):
                api_key_value = self.api_key.get_secret_value()
            else:
                api_key_value = str(self.api_key)
        logger.debug(f"Final api_key_value type: {type(api_key_value)}, value: {'***' if api_key_value else None}")

        # Handle model_kwargs and ensure api_key doesn't conflict
        model_kwargs = self.model_kwargs or {}
        # Remove api_key from model_kwargs if it exists to prevent conflicts
        if "api_key" in model_kwargs:
            logger.warning("api_key found in model_kwargs, removing to prevent conflicts")
            model_kwargs = dict(model_kwargs)  # Make a copy
            del model_kwargs["api_key"]

        parameters = {
            "api_key": api_key_value,
            "model_name": self.model_name,
            "max_tokens": self.max_tokens or None,
            "model_kwargs": model_kwargs,
            "base_url": self.openai_api_base or "https://api.openai.com/v1",
            "max_retries": self.max_retries,
            "timeout": self.timeout,
        }

        # TODO: Revisit if/once parameters are supported for reasoning models
        unsupported_params_for_reasoning_models = ["temperature", "seed"]

        if self.model_name not in OPENAI_REASONING_MODEL_NAMES:
            parameters["temperature"] = self.temperature if self.temperature is not None else 0.1
            parameters["seed"] = self.seed
        else:
            params_str = ", ".join(unsupported_params_for_reasoning_models)
            logger.debug(f"{self.model_name} is a reasoning model, {params_str} are not configurable. Ignoring.")

        # Ensure all parameter values are the correct types
        if isinstance(parameters.get("api_key"), SecretStr):
            parameters["api_key"] = parameters["api_key"].get_secret_value()
        output = ChatOpenAI(**parameters)
        if self.json_mode:
            output = output.bind(response_format={"type": "json_object"})

        return output

    def _get_exception_message(self, e: Exception):
        """Get a message from an OpenAI exception.

        Args:
            e (Exception): The exception to get the message from.

        Returns:
            str: The message from the exception.
        """
        try:
            from openai import BadRequestError
        except ImportError:
            return None
        if isinstance(e, BadRequestError):
            message = e.body.get("message")
            if message:
                return message
        return None

    def update_build_config(self, build_config: dict, field_value: Any, field_name: str | None = None) -> dict:
        if field_name in {"base_url", "model_name", "api_key"} and field_value in OPENAI_REASONING_MODEL_NAMES:
            build_config["temperature"]["show"] = False
            build_config["seed"]["show"] = False
            # Hide system_message for o1 models - currently unsupported
            if field_value.startswith("o1") and "system_message" in build_config:
                build_config["system_message"]["show"] = False
        if field_name in {"base_url", "model_name", "api_key"} and field_value in OPENAI_CHAT_MODEL_NAMES:
            build_config["temperature"]["show"] = True
            build_config["seed"]["show"] = True
            if "system_message" in build_config:
                build_config["system_message"]["show"] = True
        return build_config

    async def message_response(self) -> Message:
        # Ensure files is a list and filter out empty/None values
        files = self.files if self.files else []
        if files and not isinstance(files, list):
            files = [files]
        # Filter out None/empty values
        files = [f for f in files if f is not None and f != ""]

        session_id = self.session_id or self.graph.session_id or ""
        message = await Message.create(
            text=self.input_value,
            sender=self.sender,
            sender_name=self.sender_name,
            session_id=session_id,
            context_id=self.context_id,
            files=files,
        )
        if session_id and isinstance(message, Message) and self.should_store_message:
            stored_message = await self.send_message(
                message,
            )
            self.message.value = stored_message
            message = stored_message

        self.status = message
        return message

    inputs = [

            input_types=["Data", "JSON", "DataFrame", "Table", "Message"],

        ),

        ),
        BoolInput(

            display_name="Basic Clean Data",
            value=True,

        ),
    ]
    outputs = [
        Output(
            display_name="Output Message",
            name="message",
            method="message_response",
        ),
    ]

    def _build_source(self, id_: str | None, display_name: str | None, source: str | None) -> Source:
        source_dict = {}
        if id_:
            source_dict["id"] = id_
        if display_name:
            source_dict["display_name"] = display_name
        if source:
            # Handle case where source is a ChatOpenAI object
            if hasattr(source, "model_name"):
                source_dict["source"] = source.model_name
            elif hasattr(source, "model"):
                source_dict["source"] = str(source.model)
            else:
                source_dict["source"] = str(source)
        return Source(**source_dict)

    async def message_response(self) -> Message:
        # First convert the input to string if needed
        text = self.convert_to_string()

        # Get source properties
        source, _, display_name, source_id = self.get_properties_from_source_component()

        # Create or use existing Message object
        if isinstance(self.input_value, Message) and not self.is_connected_to_chat_input():
            message = self.input_value
            # Update message properties
            message.text = text
            # Preserve existing session_id from the incoming message if it exists
            existing_session_id = message.session_id
        else:
            message = Message(text=text)
            existing_session_id = None

        # Set message properties
        message.sender = self.sender
        message.sender_name = self.sender_name
        # Preserve session_id from incoming message, or use component/graph session_id
        message.session_id = (
            self.session_id or existing_session_id or (self.graph.session_id if hasattr(self, "graph") else None) or ""
        )
        message.context_id = self.context_id
        message.flow_id = self.graph.flow_id if hasattr(self, "graph") else None
        message.properties.source = self._build_source(source_id, display_name, source)

        # Store message if needed
        if message.session_id and self.should_store_message:
            stored_message = await self.send_message(message)
            self.message.value = stored_message
            message = stored_message

        # Set accumulated token usage from all upstream LLM vertices.
        # This must happen AFTER send_message() because streaming captures
        # usage from chunks and would overwrite accumulated totals.
        if hasattr(self, "_vertex") and self._vertex is not None:
            accumulated_usage = self._vertex._accumulate_upstream_token_usage()  # noqa: SLF001
            if accumulated_usage:
                message.properties.usage = accumulated_usage
                if self.should_store_message and message.get_id():
                    message = await self._update_stored_message(message)
                    await self._send_message_event(message, id_=message.get_id())

        self.status = message
        return message

    def _serialize_data(self, data: Data) -> str:
        """Serialize Data object to JSON string."""
        # Convert data.data to JSON-serializable format
        serializable_data = jsonable_encoder(data.data)
        # Serialize with orjson, enabling pretty printing with indentation
        json_bytes = orjson.dumps(serializable_data, option=orjson.OPT_INDENT_2)
        # Convert bytes to string and wrap in Markdown code blocks
        return "```json\n" + json_bytes.decode("utf-8") + "\n```"

    def _validate_input(self) -> None:
        """Validate the input data and raise ValueError if invalid."""
        if self.input_value is None:
            msg = "Input data cannot be None"
            raise ValueError(msg)
        if isinstance(self.input_value, list) and not all(
            isinstance(item, Message | Data | DataFrame | str) for item in self.input_value
        ):
            invalid_types = [
                type(item).__name__
                for item in self.input_value
                if not isinstance(item, Message | Data | DataFrame | str)
            ]
            msg = f"Expected Data or DataFrame or Message or str, got {invalid_types}"
            raise TypeError(msg)
        if not isinstance(
            self.input_value,
            Message | Data | DataFrame | str | list | Generator | type(None),
        ):
            type_name = type(self.input_value).__name__
            msg = f"Expected Data or DataFrame or Message or str, Generator or None, got {type_name}"
            raise TypeError(msg)

    def convert_to_string(self) -> str | Generator[Any, None, None]:
        """Convert input data to string with proper error handling."""
        self._validate_input()
        if isinstance(self.input_value, list):
            clean_data: bool = getattr(self, "clean_data", False)
            return "\n".join([safe_convert(item, clean_data=clean_data) for item in self.input_value])
        if isinstance(self.input_value, Generator):
            return self.input_value
        return safe_convert(self.input_value)
